title: Scope chat API to current user and companion in chatbot/api/chat.py
description:
Modify chatbot/api/chat.py to scope all chat operations to the authenticated user and optionally to a companion. Apply get_current_user dependency and enforce user_id ownership on session access and chat message storage.

Before editing, inspect:
- AGENTS.md
- docs/plans_tasks.md
- docs/operations.md
- docs/architecture.md
- docs/PLANS/ACTIVE/CHATBOT/README.md
- docs/PLANS/ACTIVE/CHATBOT/DISPATCH.md
- chatbot/api/chat.py (existing chat API — understand current endpoints, request/response models, router name, and how sessions are used)
- chatbot/auth/dependencies.py (created by task c.5 — get_current_user, CurrentUser)
- chatbot/db/models.py (updated by task c.4 — Session and ChatMessage models with user_id/companion_id columns)
- chatbot/companions/companion.py (created by task c.3 — CompanionManager)

Do not infer APIs, constructor signatures, function names, module locations, or service topology from the task description alone. Inspect the referenced documents and existing implementation files first, then implement against the actual repository.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY chatbot/api/chat.py. Do NOT modify any other file under any circumstance. Do NOT update documentation, READMEs, operations guides, or any code outside the listed path. If you believe other files need updating, ignore that impulse and finish the task with only the listed file modified. Out-of-scope edits will cause the task to be rejected.

Implementation details:

1. Open chatbot/api/chat.py and understand:
   - Current endpoints and their signatures.
   - How the session_id is validated (in-memory lookup, database, etc.).
   - Router variable name, prefix, and tag.
   - How chat messages/turns are stored.
   - Request/response model definitions (ChatRequest, ChatResponse, etc.).

2. Add user_id scoping:
   - Import `get_current_user` from chatbot.auth.dependencies.
   - Add `current_user: CurrentUser = Depends(get_current_user)` to every endpoint.
   - Before processing any chat message, validate that the session belongs to the current user. If not found or owned by a different user, return 404.
   - Store user_id from current_user on all created chat messages/turns.

3. Add companion support:
   - Accept optional companion_id in the chat request body.
   - If companion_id is provided, validate it exists and is owned by the current user (use CompanionManager). If not, return 404.
   - Store companion_id on chat messages/turns.
   - The session's companion_id (if set) should match the request's companion_id (if both are set), otherwise return 400.

4. Do NOT modify the chat pipeline execution logic, TurnContext, TurnPipeline, or any pipeline step code — only add auth scoping around the existing logic.

5. Do NOT rename the router, change endpoint URL paths, or change HTTP methods.
acceptance_criteria: chatbot/api/chat.py imports and uses get_current_user dependency on all endpoints
Chat endpoint verifies session belongs to current_user before processing
Chat endpoint returns 404 when session is not owned by the authenticated user
Chat messages/turns are stored with user_id from current_user
Chat endpoint accepts optional companion_id and validates ownership
Chat endpoint returns 404 when companion_id is provided but not found or not owned by user
Existing endpoint paths, router name, and prefix are preserved
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: rename the router or change existing endpoint URL paths
change the chat pipeline or step execution logic
return 200 for chat against sessions owned by a different user
change the Abracapocus runtime, orchestrator, or backends

allowed: add Depends(get_current_user) to existing endpoint signatures
validate session ownership before processing chat messages
validate companion ownership when companion_id is provided
store user_id and companion_id on chat message records
forbidden: change existing endpoint URL paths or HTTP methods
remove existing chat functionality (pipeline execution, response generation)
modify TurnContext, TurnPipeline, or pipeline step logic
return 200 or 403 for unauthorized session access (use 404 to prevent enumeration)
